# openjpeg / opj_decompress_fuzzer_JP2

openjpeg's own fuzz target `opj_decompress_fuzzer_JP2` ([source](source/opj_decompress_fuzzer_JP2.cpp), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over openjpeg (uclouvain/openjpeg at 402ef586).

Accepts only a JP2 file whose bytes 4..7 are the 'jP ' box; opj_read_header, then opj_set_decode_area clamped to 1024x1024 and opj_decode from a memory stream; the decoded image is never inspected.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against openjpeg at commit 402ef586.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
The harness makes no check of its own beyond not crashing. Its halts statements say only that the code it calls never crashes, hangs or trips a sanitizer. Its agreement statements say only that the code never crashes or trips a sanitizer, and allow a run that never ends. Its bound statements say only how often its builds may disagree. Its decidability statements say only that some program decides where its builds agree.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch openjpeg` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `opj_decompress_fuzzer_JP2.plain` | 289,752 | `9aa7bf255b2bf5bd2ce262aa296d6c504433cb719b36d14f7e932de8585645cf` |
| ubsan | `opj_decompress_fuzzer_JP2.ubsan` | 360,016 | `ae4eb9c1a04a9aad430a647e57a3e616880b628285674d3ceb89b61aa5f236b0` |
| asan | `opj_decompress_fuzzer_JP2.asan` | 1,382,040 | `0f5491d34f467ff2290f58ce0ecf01ceb3c4396abc9e62047165199cef39d7a6` |
| asan-ubsan | `opj_decompress_fuzzer_JP2.asan-ubsan` | 1,456,952 | `ce385b2c9b585cdfd7c16c2c58b520823950f5f260edbc4349fff3282cf5a094` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
